root_motivation: **Who:** the agent whose client renders resources (Claude Code `@mcphost:…`, VS Code Copilot "Add Context", Cursor); the human user who wants the run log in the chat without asking the agent to fetch it. **What:** read a table, a doc, a run log or a tool spec by URI, and be told when it changes. **Why not today:** prod answers `resources/list` with `{"resources":[]}` (rmcp default); after PRD-mcphost-server-capabilities-from-registry it answers `-32601`. Every read is a `tools/call` with `tenant_key` in `arguments`; the resource methods have no arguments slot for a key, so the auth that `list_tools` performs (`handler.rs:7838-7850`: path secret first, then `resolve_auth` over header and connection) is the only auth available — nothing today proves it reaches `read_resource`. **Consequence:** the explore personas re-implement reads as tool calls (`usecases.py` 10-08: 26 `budget.max_tool_latency_ms` refusals came from agents polling `host.table.query` for data a subscription would...
user_persona: An agent that runs host.note.put {text, attach_to: {tool}} once and reads the note on that tool's description in every later session; the same user's second client sees it too.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given an in-process server with a path-bound tenant `/u/{secret}/mcp` that owns table `orders` with 3 rows, When `resources/read mcphost://table/orders` is sent on that connection, Then the result's single content is `application/json` with 3 rows; Given a keyless connection that never signed up, When the same URI is read, Then `-32002` is returned and the tenants table gained 0 rows.

Given `RESOURCE_TEMPLATES`, When `resources/templates/list` is sent keyless, Then it lists exactly the const's rows with `uriTemplate` and `mimeType`; Given `docs/protocol/resources.md`, Then its table equals the const byte-for-byte.

Given a tenant with 2 tables, 1 doc, 1 run, 2 tools, When `resources/list` is sent with the key in the Authorization header, Then 6 entries are returned; Given an OAuth session scoped `tables:read`, Then exactly the 2 table entries.

Given a subscription on `mcphost://table/orders`, When `host.table.append` commits 2 rows, Then one `notifications/resources/updated {uri}` reaches the peer within 500 ms; Given `unsubscribe`, Then a further append sends nothing.

Given a free tenant with 8 open subscriptions, When the 9th `resources/subscribe` arrives, Then `resources_max` is returned with `data.limit: 8`; Given the connection closes, Then all 8 entries are gone and a new connection may open 8 again.

Given a table whose JSON exceeds `resource_read_bytes_max`, When read, Then the body is cut at the last complete row under the ceiling and `_meta.truncated` is `true`; Given another tenant's table name, Then `-32002`, never `forbidden`.

Given `capabilities.rs`, When `initialize` is answered, Then `capabilities.resources` is `{listChanged: true, subscribe: true}` and `/capabilities.json` shows `resources.implemented == true`, `probe == "resources"`.

scope: src/notes.rs: host.note.put/list/delete over the notes/ prefix of tenant_state_kv; the tools/list description suffix.
src/handler.rs, src/protocol/frames.rs: tools, dispatch, list_changed on a tool-attached put/delete (keyed row allows list_changed).
src/plans.rs, src/retention.rs, src/db.rs: notes_max plan field; expired-note sweep.
contracts/, docs/, www/: regenerated tool contract, output schemas, docs.
non_goals: Notes attached to runs surfaced in host.runs.get (R6), attached_to in host.resume/welcome_back (R5), pin (R7); shared notebooks across tenants.

additional.engine_form: mcphost-qjs subprocess in the python bwrap profile; cold_p95_ms measured by jsk_ac01

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the next session repeat a mistake the last one learned from?
five_whys_trace.a: The only write path is remember at signup; nothing pins a note to the tool it is about.
